title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 60
paragraphs: In the following respect too the Lacedaemonians resemble the Egyptians: their heralds, flute-players, and cooks inherit the crafts of their fathers, and a flute-player is the son of a flute-player, a cook of a cook, and a herald of a herald. Other men do not lay hands on the office because they have loud and clear voices and so shut them out of it; they practice their craft by inheritance from their fathers.
